Description: A Society Hill landmark for modern Israeli cooking. Dinner starts with silky hummus, a spread of salatim and laffa bread from the wood-fired oven, and the pomegranate-glazed lamb shoulder is built for sharing.
An intimate townhouse dining room serving a multi-course Italian tasting menu. Handmade pastas like spinach gnocchi and almond tortellini have made it one of the city's special-occasion favorites.
The South Philly corner stand that claims to have invented the cheesesteak in 1930. Order at the window, say "wit" or "witout" for onions, and eat at the outdoor counters any hour of the day.
Pat's neon-lit rival across the intersection at 9th and Passyunk. Thin-sliced ribeye on a fresh roll, served around the clock since 1966.
A Roxborough neighborhood shop where the beef is chopped fine on the griddle and piled high. Locals swear by it, so expect a line at lunch and grab a seat at the counter if you can.
A bustling Parisian-style brasserie on Rittenhouse Square with sidewalk tables, warm baskets of bread and classic bistro dishes from breakfast through late dinner.
A lively Midtown Village wine bar with Mediterranean small plates, wood-fired pizzas and the famous salted caramel budino.
A Chinatown favorite for Shanghai-style soup dumplings. Bite a small hole, sip the broth, then try the pan-fried noodles and scallion pancakes.
Chef Cristina Martinez's Italian Market taqueria, known for slow-cooked lamb barbacoa served in fresh tortillas with consomme on the side.
A Lebanese restaurant, market and garden in Fishtown. Fresh-baked man'oushe, colorful mezze and grilled kebabs come out of an open kitchen into a beautiful courtyard.
Chef Nok Suntaranon's Southern Thai restaurant in a soaring, plant-filled Fishtown dining room. Curries are bold and spicy, and dishes are made for passing around the table.
An Israeli-style skewer house in Kensington. Choose a grilled skewer and the table fills up with salatim, hummus and pita, with soft-serve to finish.
Chef Greg Vernick's Rittenhouse townhouse restaurant, where seasonal toasts, raw bar plates and wood-roasted dishes are served at a warm, buzzy bar and dining room.
A Mediterranean taverna on the Avenue of the Arts known for whole fish grilled over charcoal and sold by the pound, with live music on weekend nights.
A family-run Center City raw bar with a long marble counter, a wall of vintage oyster plates and a daily list of East Coast oysters.
A Chinatown favorite run by the Lai family since 1984, serving a dozen kinds of pho, grilled-meat vermicelli bowls and crispy spring rolls in a cozy two-floor dining room.
Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto's sleek Old City dining room with a glowing, color-changing interior, creative sushi and a signature omakase.
A Center City spot for South Indian specialties, from paper-thin dosas and fluffy idli to fragrant biryani and Chettinad curries.
A Lower East Side deli serving hand-carved pastrami since 1888. Hold on to your ticket, tip the cutter and get ready for a sandwich stacked a mile high.
A Williamsburg steakhouse open since 1887, famous for dry-aged porterhouse for two, thick-cut bacon and old-school waiters.
A Greenwich Village slice counter serving classic thin, foldable New York slices since 1975. Grab a plain slice and eat it on the sidewalk.
Known as America's first pizzeria, this Nolita spot bakes whole pies in a coal oven. Cash only and well worth the wait.
Chef Eric Ripert's elegant Midtown temple to seafood, where nearly raw and lightly cooked fish are served with refined French sauces.
A grand SoHo brasserie with red banquettes, antique mirrors and towering seafood platters, open from breakfast until late.
A family-run appetizing shop since 1914, selling smoked fish, bagels and schmears across a long counter on the Lower East Side.
OwnerName: Niki Russ Federman & Josh Russ Tupper

Description: A loud, proud Lower East Side restaurant inside Essex Market that serves the regional Indian dishes rarely found on restaurant menus.
Hand-ripped noodles and spicy cumin lamb from western China. The Chinatown shop is fast, casual and full of chili oil.
A standing-room taco counter inside Chelsea Market with handmade corn tortillas, adobada carved off the spit and quick-moving lines.
An Atlantic City sub shop open since 1946, serving giant Italian subs on fresh-baked rolls. Photos of famous customers cover the walls.
A family-owned Atlantic City seafood house, open since 1897, with a raw bar, live piano music and nightly happy hour.
A South Jersey institution with a huge menu, an in-house bakery and a dessert case that's hard to walk past.
A modern, chrome-trimmed diner with an enormous menu and plates sized to share. Breakfast and desserts are the big draws.
Chef Dan Richer's Jersey City pizzeria, known for naturally leavened crust, house-made mozzarella and bread and butter worth ordering on its own.
A wood-fired BYOB on Haddon Avenue where most of the menu is cooked over an open hearth. Bring a bottle and settle in.
The original brewpub of Delaware's best-known craft brewery, pouring beers brewed on site next to wood-fired pizzas, burgers and sandwiches.
A downtown Wilmington gastropub across from the Grand Opera House, with brick-oven pizzas, a long craft beer list and a late-night kitchen.
A historic stone inn on Pennsylvania Avenue serving modern American dinners and a popular Sunday brunch.
A busy Rehoboth seafood restaurant with its own fish market. Fresh catches are grilled, blackened or broiled to order.
A Delaware beach tradition since 1960, known for its sweet sauce swirled on top of the cheese.
A North Wilmington steakhouse since 1988, famous for slow-roasted prime rib, aged steaks and a lively bar.
